question: What is the main focus of systems thinking in healthcare?

options.A: Viewing the clinical environment as an interconnected network
options.B: Punishing healthcare workers who make clinical mistakes
options.C: Focusing exclusively on individual performance during procedures
options.D: Reducing the overall salary budget for hospital staff members

explanation: Systems thinking focuses on how various elements in the clinical environment interact rather than looking at events in isolation. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h1)

question: A nurse makes a medication error. What would a systems thinker investigate first?

options.A: The exact speed at which the nurse completed the shift
options.B: The personal background and academic history of the nurse
options.C: The specific disciplinary action outlined in hospital policy
options.D: The environmental and structural factors that allowed the error

explanation: A systems approach examines the underlying workplace conditions and processes that made the mistake possible. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which item represents an input in a healthcare system?

options.B: The clinical procedure for changing a wound dressing
options.C: The administrative workflow for discharging clients
options.D: The final patient recovery rate after surgery

explanation: Inputs are the structural resources like staff and equipment put into the system to enable care delivery. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of identifying boundaries in a healthcare system?

options.A: To prevent student nurses from entering intensive care units
options.B: To separate internal ward operations from external influences
options.C: To eliminate the need for interprofessional communication
options.D: To restrict patients from accessing specialized medical doctors

explanation: Boundaries define what falls under internal operational control versus external environmental factors. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h2)

question: What does interdependence mean in the context of a hospital system?

options.A: Different departments rely on each other to function properly
options.B: Every hospital ward must operate completely independently
options.C: Individual nurses are solely responsible for patient recovery
options.D: Administrative staff control all clinical nursing decisions

explanation: Interdependence means that the actions and outputs of one department directly affect the operations of another. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h3)

question: A delay in laboratory test results halts the administration of prescribed antibiotics. What does this situation illustrate?

options.A: A deliberate failure in individual nursing competence
options.B: A chain reaction caused by system interdependence
options.C: An unnecessary waste of hospital financial resources
options.D: An isolated event with no impact on patient care

explanation: When one component stalls, it triggers disruptions across other connected parts of the healthcare delivery network. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h3)

question: What defines common cause variation in healthcare processes?

options.A: Normal, expected fluctuations in everyday clinical tasks
options.B: Severe equipment breakdowns during a major surgical procedure
options.C: Sudden power outages affecting the entire hospital compound
options.D: Intentional policy violations committed by individual staff

explanation: Common cause variations are the natural, predictable differences inherent in routine daily operations. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which scenario is an example of special cause variation?

options.A: A brand-new infusion pump model failing without staff orientation
options.B: Normal variations in patient vital signs across a twenty-four hour shift
options.C: Slight daily differences in the duration of morning bed baths
options.D: Routine waiting times experienced during busy outpatient clinic hours

explanation: Special cause variations stem from unusual, unexpected events that fall outside normal operating conditions. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is a latent condition in a healthcare system?

options.A: A hidden system weakness that exists long before an error occurs
options.B: A temporary staff shortage happening during a single shift
options.C: A direct, intentional violation of hospital rules by a nurse
options.D: An unexpected recovery following a terminal medical diagnosis

explanation: Latent conditions are pre-existing flaws in design, equipment, or policy that lie dormant in the system. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h5)

question: Why is root cause analysis preferred over simply blaming an individual worker?

options.A: It uncovers and corrects underlying systemic flaws
options.B: It allows the hospital to avoid filing legal incident reports
options.C: It guarantees that no clinical mistakes will ever happen again
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing new medical supplies

explanation: Root cause analysis digs deep into workplace processes to fix the actual environmental factors causing errors. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h5)

question: What does the SBAR communication tool stand to improve in a healthcare system?

options.A: The physical layout and architectural design of emergency wards
options.B: The speed at which hospital financial budgets are approved
options.C: Standardized and structured communication across clinical departments
options.D: The recruitment process for hiring new administrative personnel

explanation: SBAR provides a clear, shared framework for transmitting vital patient information safely between healthcare providers. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h6)

question: A nurse notices two different injectable medications with nearly identical label designs in the treatment room. What is the most appropriate systems-based action to take?

options.A: Report the design flaw to management to prevent administration errors
options.B: Ignore the packaging because experienced nurses never make mistakes
options.C: Hide one of the medication vials in a private desk drawer
options.D: Blame the junior nursing colleagues for not reading labels carefully

explanation: Reporting a design hazard helps fix a latent system condition before it leads to an adverse patient event. [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h6)
